newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Taylor Woodrow gears up for buys.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Taylor Woodrow gears up for buys.

text.p: Taylor Woodrow Plc, the UK construction to housebuilding group, said on Tuesday it was prepared to gear up to 40 percent to fund further acquisitions for growth.
Colin Parsons, chairman, told Reuters in an interview: "We are currently low at 11 percent. We don't expect to keep it as low as that," adding that it could go up to 30 or 40 percent.
Its wholesale business Greenham Trading would be best expanded through organic growth but there was potential to make buys for Taylor Woodrow's housing and property development divisions, he said.
On the outlook for housing, the group's star performer in the 1996 results, the chairman said that he did not see the possible change of government in the UK as a threat.
The most pressing concern in UK housing is land price inflation. "Land prices in the UK are high. It is very difficult."
He said that could cause problems unless house prices rose to reflect the underlying land values in the near future.
On the possibility of an interest rate rise in the U.S., Parsons said: "If it's just by a small amount it would have no effect, but a bigger rise would be very concerning."
The other key feature of the results was the construction unit's move into a tiny profit from major losses last year.

He said construction remained competitive and that the group had limited its downside by remaining extremely selective about projects and terms. But there were signs of improvement in the UK market, he said.
